correctness.rationale: Anchor the Gram matrix at the attachment vertex. The mean-zero unmarked-clique and leaf sectors have eigenvalues 1/2 and q/2. On the remaining sector, using total load on each class, the Gram form has diagonal U_m and 1−β_n q and off-diagonal 1−q/2. Its determinant times four is F(q)=4U_m(1−β_n q)−(q−2)^2. It is positive at q=1,2 and negative at 1/β_n; strict concavity and its negative leading coefficient give one crossing for q≥1 and no later return. The positive pivot gives a one-dimensional kernel there, with class totals ((Q−2)/(2U_m),1) and their negative sum at the hub; rank gives the claimed affine dimensions. At a root 1−β_n Q>0, so decreasing U_m or increasing β_n decreases the upper crossing strictly. For ε=1/n and δ=Q−2 the equation is δ²+2U_m(1−ε)δ−4U_m ε=0. Its δ derivative at ε=δ=0 is bounded away from zero on U_m∈[1/2,3/4]; expansion gives δ=2ε+(−2+4/m)ε²+O(ε³) uniformly, and the logarithm gives the asserted second coefficient. The frozen script and notes were inspected, not executed. The separately written `python /workspace/branches/independent_reproduction.py 1` passed below/at/above full anchored Gram signs and nullity for 12 independently reconstructed shortest-path instances; the formulas, not the finite sample, prove the family theorem.
